stepTitle: Does this decomposition hold true for classification decision trees and zero-one loss? (Zero-one loss is equal to $$1$$ if a prediction is correct, and $$0$$ if it is incorrect.)
stepBody: In class, we derived the following bias-variance decomposition under a specific set of conditions.\nmodel risk $$=$$ $$\sigma**{2}+(\text{bias})**{2}+\text{variance}$$\nWe assume that there is an unknown underlying function $$g(x)$$ that generates the points we observe. Specifically, we observe $$Y_i=g(x_i)+\epsilon_i$$ where $$\epsilon_i$$ is a zero-mean noise term with variance $$\sigma**{2}$$ that is independent for each observation. Our model's goal is to approximate $$g(x)$$ as best as possible.
